# Critterkit

> Critterkit gives a web or iOS app an animated, AI-painted mascot that reacts to what people do: it watches typing, points at invalid fields, cheers successful saves, worries about errors, and celebrates moments like streaks and purchases. One script tag on the web, one Swift package on iOS.

Each mascot has an id (for example "xyjv3nf5en3k"). Create one at https://www.critterkit.com/paint. Leave `mascot` out to use the free drawn mascot.

## Web install

Load the script once, then render the tag once near the end of <body>:

```html
<script src="https://www.critterkit.com/critter.js"></script>
<critter-mascot mascot="YOUR_MASCOT_ID" autopilot greet></critter-mascot>
```

- `autopilot`: floats in a corner and reacts to the page on its own (typing, password fields, invalid forms, slow/failed/successful fetch and XHR requests, error messages, rage taps, tab return, offline/online). Do not rebuild these by hand.
- `greet`: says hello on load. `greeting="Hi!"` sets the line.
- `dock="#selector"`: lives inside that element instead of a corner, and steps out when it needs to.
- `position` (bottom-right, bottom-left, top-right, top-left), `size`, `mobile-size`, `offset`.

React / Next.js: it is a standard web component. In JSX write boolean attributes as `autopilot="" greet=""`. In Next.js load the script with `next/script` and `strategy="afterInteractive"` in the root layout. For TypeScript:

```ts
declare namespace JSX { interface IntrinsicElements { 'critter-mascot': any } }
```

## Web API

```js
const pip = document.querySelector('critter-mascot')

pip.moment('first-purchase')
pip.moment('streak', { count: 7 })          // bigger celebrations at 7, 30, 100…
pip.moment('level-up', { count: 5 })
pip.moment('milestone', { say: '100 notes written!', at: '#notes' })

pip.goTo(el, { mode: 'point' | 'sit', state: 'success', text: 'Nice!', stay: false })
pip.point(el, 'This one is missing')
pip.tour([{ target: '#plan', text: 'Pick a plan' }], { done: 'You are set!' })
pip.react('love', 2000)                    // temporary reaction
pip.setState('thinking')                   // held until changed
pip.say('Saved!', { hold: 1500 })
pip.home(); pip.lookAt(x, y); pip.cover(true)
pip.hideMascot(); pip.showMascot()

pip.play([
  { do: 'flip' },
  { do: 'react', state: 'dance', ms: 2500 },
  { do: 'say', text: 'Level {level}!' },
  { do: 'emote', kind: 'spark' }
], { level: user.level })
```

Moments: first-purchase, purchase, streak, milestone, level-up, goal, welcome, welcome-back, empty, oops. Each accepts `say` to override the line and `at` (selector or element) to celebrate next to something.

States and reactions: idle, thinking, success, error, surprised, confused, love, wave, talking, sleeping, dance, sad, peek.

play steps (each waits until done): jump, bigjump, flip, spin, shake, grow, poof (with `to`: home, center, left, right, random or a selector), goto (with `target`), moment (with `name`), react (with `state`, `ms`), say (with `text`), emote (with `kind`: spark, note, dust, bang, sweat, smoke, drops, confetti, hearts), prop (with `emoji`, `ms`), wait (with `ms`). `{placeholders}` in text are filled from the second argument.

Events: `ready`, `error` (painted mascot failed to load), `statechange` (detail.state), `pip:autopilot` (detail.action, detail.signal), `pip:hide`, `pip:show`.

No-code moments: the mascot's owner can set rules on critterkit.com/mascots (visit a path, tap a button by its text, or words appearing on the page -> a moment, a line, pointing at a button, or a play sequence). critter.js runs them automatically; add `no-rules` to turn them off. If the user only wants simple celebrations on a website, this may be easier than code.

## iOS (SwiftUI / UIKit)

Swift package: https://github.com/corylarro/CritterKit

```swift
import CritterKit

ContentView()
  .critterMascot(.init(mascotID: "YOUR_MASCOT_ID"))

TextField("Email", text: $email).critterTarget("email")

Critter.moment(.firstPurchase)
Critter.moment(.streak(days: 7))
Critter.moment(.levelUp(5))
Critter.moment(.milestone, say: "100 notes!", at: "notes")
Critter.point(at: "email", say: "That email looks off.")
try await Critter.watch(success: "Saved!") { try await save() }
Critter.react(.love); Critter.say("Hi!"); Critter.set(.thinking); Critter.home()
Critter.play([["do": "flip"], ["do": "say", "text": "Level {level}!"]], values: ["level": level])
```

UIKit: `Critter.start(.init(mascotID: "YOUR_MASCOT_ID"))`.

## Guidance for AI coding tools

- Add the mascot once, globally. Use moments only for real events (purchase, streak, goal, level, first visit, empty state, failure), not on every click.
- Keep lines short and in the app's voice.
- Autopilot already handles forms, requests and errors.
